correctness.rationale: For Brownian diffusion D>0 and nonzero deterministic |a|=c<1 Poisson proportional resets rate r>0, stationary X=sum_{j>=0}a^j Z_j with independent Laplace variables of scale ell=sqrt(D/r). Characteristic function product∏(1+ell² c^{2j}u²)^-1 decays faster than every inverse polynomial (select arbitrarily many fixed factors), yielding C^infinity via Fourier inversion. Stationary adjoint pantograph equation at x=0 gives f^(2n)(0)=(-1)^n f(0)ell^(-2n)c^(-n²)∏_{j<n}(1-c^(2j+1)), with all odd derivatives zero; independent exact-rational recurrence checks passed 48 cases. Derivative growth exp(Ln²+O(n)) for L=-log c prohibits every finite Gevrey order and gives zero Taylor radius. Known exponential-density series converges holomorphically in Re z>0 (reflected on negative line), so zero is the sole nonanalytic point. Cosine Taylor remainder bounded by absolute 2n moment, taking n=floor(log(ell/|x|)/L) yields f(0)exp(L-t²/L). The stationary single-time density claim does not extend to |a|=0 or >=1.
residual_risks: Convergence of the known residue series was checked by mathematical coefficient bounds; numerical checks do not certify full regularity.
The special case a=0 is a Laplace density with cusp; |a|=1 lacks stationary probability.

value.rationale: Distinguishing global C-infinity regularity from extreme nonanalyticity at the stationary peak is a mathematically meaningful regularity phase change. The exact jet and explicit super-algebraic approximation by logarithmically many Taylor terms quantify this counterintuitive structure, which a researcher analyzing local reset distributions can use.
residual_risks: Known stationary density and smoothness by themselves are not novel; value is attached to the rigorous all-order regularity and approximation dichotomy.

scientific_limitations: Strictly contractive deterministic nonzero multiplier, Brownian noise, Poisson resets, one-point stationary law.
